pr_title: importer: add deprecation notice for mysqldump/pgdump
pr_body:
fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/93660

Release note (sql change): The PGDUMP and MYSQLDUMP formats for IMPORT were marked as deprecated. They are still present, but will be removed in a future release. The page at https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v22.2/migration-overview shows alternatives.

issue_context.title: sql: deprecate IMPORT PGDUMP/MYSQLDUMP
issue_context.body:
Starting with 23.1, we should deprecate PGDUMP/MYSQLDUMP by showing a deprecation message to de-emphasize usage. This should direct users to a doc page that outlines alternative methods of data ingestion into Cockroach DB. The easiest method would be to pipe the pgdump into the Cockroach CLI, which will handle the data and schema together; however, we should emphasize the following:

We should point to using the Schema Conversion Tool for the schema portion.
We should suggest either using COPY to export a table into CSV in the case of Postgres or SELECT INTO OUTFILE for exporting a CSV for a table in the case of MySQL. Depending on the requirements, this CSV can then be ingested via either COPY or IMPORT.


Jira issue: CRDB-22454
comments:
For the docs link, I think we can just reuse this page:
https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/v22.2/migration-overview

Might have to pin the version to the database version 23.1 somehow in the actual deprecation message, however.

review_comments: The message looks good to me. Does this also handle: `IMPORT TABLE 'foo' FROM PGDUMP`?
yeah, that will show the notice too. there is a test for it.
